answer.sourceLine: The three-sentence takeover claim is unconfirmed as Khrushchev’s. Wikiquote marks it disputed and notes its online circulation; his documented 1956 “We will bury you” remark is a different statement and does not authenticate these added sentences.

author.name: Nikita Khrushchev
author.heading: About Nikita Khrushchev
author.bio: Nikita Khrushchev led the Soviet Communist Party from 1953 to 1964 and served as Soviet premier from 1958. His leadership combined the denunciation of Stalin’s abuses with Cold War confrontations, including the Cuban Missile Crisis.

cite.sourceCitation: “We will take America without firing a shot …,” disputed attribution to Nikita Khrushchev, documented by Wikiquote. Compared with the separate November 18, 1956 “We will bury you” remark; no primary source for the three-sentence passage located.
cite.pageCitation: Quotle.info. “Who really said ‘We will take America without firing a shot. We do not have to invade the U.S. We will destroy you from within’?” Last verified 9 Nov 2026.

misattribution.truthLine: Keep the attribution unconfirmed; no original author is established.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The passage promises an internal collapse rather than an invasion, which makes it adaptable to arguments about later American political conflicts. Its familiar Cold War attribution lends that interpretation the appearance of a prediction.

The separate 1956 remark cannot serve as a source for additional sentences simply because their message seems similar. A date attached to a meme is a claim to be checked, not a substitute for a speech text or recording.

schema.faqAnswer: The three-sentence takeover claim is unconfirmed as Khrushchev’s. Wikiquote marks it disputed and notes its online circulation; his documented 1956 “We will bury you” remark is a different statement and does not authenticate these added sentences.
